VERDICT: DISAGREE. One of exactly two pieces of cited evidence in this PR's central claim does not exist on the page it is cited to. The PR's CONCLUSION is correct and is in fact better supported by a source the PR does not cite -- so this is a citation repair, not a retraction.

== FINDING 1 (BLOCKING): a fabricated doc citation, repeated in three places, one of them the permanent risk register ==

The PR narrows finding 6 using two cited claims about https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md:

  (a) "In version 2.1.63, the Task tool was renamed to Agent. Existing `Task(...)` references in settings and agent definitions still work as aliases."
  (b) "The same page's own `PreToolUse` hook-matcher example uses exactly \"matcher\": \"Agent\" -- the same string this repo's hooks.json already ships."

(a) is TRUE, verbatim. I fetched the cited URL myself (HTTP 200, 117927 bytes) and found it at line 481, inside the section "Restrict which subagents can be spawned", word for word as quoted.

(b) is FALSE. That page contains no hook-matcher example using `Agent`, anywhere.

REPRODUCTION (any machine with network access to the docs host):
  curl -sS https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md -o sub-agents.md
  grep -c -F '"matcher": "Agent"' sub-agents.md   ->  0
  grep -c -F 'matcher: "Agent"'    sub-agents.md   ->  0
  grep -n 'matcher' sub-agents.md
    664:    - matcher: "Bash"
    756:    - matcher: "Bash"
    761:    - matcher: "Edit|Write"
    788:        "matcher": "db-agent",
    1341:    - matcher: "Bash"

Every matcher example on that page is `Bash`, `Edit|Write`, or `db-agent`. I fetched the URL twice, independently, and both bodies hash identically (sha256 65b7fa169e8d95598587af58fc55046ec956ef4f457a9a93536de72b6a697410), so this is not a transient or partial fetch.

What the page actually has near the quoted rename note is a `tools:` FRONTMATTER FIELD example -- `tools: Agent(worker, researcher), Read, Bash` -- which is an allowlist of spawnable subagent types, not a hook matcher at all. The page's only place where `Agent` and `matcher` appear near each other is lines 776-788, the SubagentStart/SubagentStop table, and that text says the opposite of what claim (b) needs: "The matcher value is the agent's frontmatter `name`", with the worked example matching `"db-agent"` -- an agent type name, not the tool name `Agent`. The PR appears to have conflated the `tools:` allowlist syntax, or the SubagentStart agent-name matcher, with a PreToolUse tool-name matcher.

WHY THIS BLOCKS, given the conclusion is right. This PR's entire deliverable IS a citation. Its product is a dated maintainers note whose value is that a later reader can follow the URL and confirm the narrowing without redoing the work. A reader who does that will find claim (b) absent and has no way to know that claim (a) -- on the same page, in the same paragraph, sourced the same way -- is sound. A false citation sitting beside a true one does not merely add nothing; it puts the true one in doubt. And this text is not confined to the new note: commit e4a14ce appends it to docs/maintainers/proof-of-completion-plan.md, this repo's standing risk register, under a convention that annotations are appended and not rewritten, which makes it durable.

It appears in three places, all needing the same repair:
  1. docs/maintainers/item-1.8-hook-matcher-name-2026-09-25.md, section "The resolution", paragraph beginning "The same page's worked example of a `PreToolUse` hook matcher intercepting subagent dispatch uses exactly ...", and again in "What this narrows" ("it is the exact string the hooks reference itself uses in a `PreToolUse` subagent-matcher example").
  2. docs/maintainers/proof-of-completion-plan.md, the PARTIALLY NARROWED 2026-09-25 annotation under finding 6.
  3. The PR description itself.

THE FIX IS ONE CITATION SWAP, AND THE CORRECT SOURCE IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE CLAIMED. https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md (fetched here, HTTP 200, 331143 bytes), in its PreToolUse section, line 1585, states directly:

  "Runs after Claude creates tool parameters and before processing the tool call. Matches on any tool name except `EndConversation`: built-in tools such as `Bash`, `PowerShell`, `Edit`, `Write`, `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Agent`, `Workflow`, `WebFetch`, `WebSearch`, `AskUserQuestion`, and `ExitPlanMode`, and any MCP tool names."

That is an explicit statement that `PreToolUse` matches the tool name `Agent` -- exactly the proposition claim (b) was reaching for, from the canonical hooks reference rather than the subagents page. Line 2428 of the same doc corroborates ("use a `PostToolUse` hook on the `Agent` tool instead"). Replacing (b) with this citation makes the note's conclusion hold on cited evidence, and I would record AGREE on a head that does so.

I note the substantive conclusion is UNAFFECTED: `Agent` is a real, current, documented tool name, claim (a) establishes the rename, and hooks.md line 1585 establishes that PreToolUse matches on it. Finding 6's dead-matcher-name half genuinely is narrowed. The defect is the evidence, not the result -- which is why this DISAGREE should cost a small commit, not a rethink.

== FINDING 2 (NON-BLOCKING): the acceptance criteria cannot fail on the false half ==

proof/lwb-item-1.8-hook-matcher-name.json's acceptance_criteria has a criterion for the rename quote ("quotes the official Anthropic doc's exact Task-renamed-to-Agent note verbatim, with the doc URL cited", met: true -- correctly) and none at all for the hook-matcher-example claim. So the record's own criteria are satisfiable with claim (b) false, and were. This is the shape this repo keeps finding: a check that passes whether or not the thing it guards is true. Worth one more criterion binding each cited quotation to its source, so a future citation claim has something that bites.

To its credit, the record's `unproven` list is genuinely honest and names precisely the hole the finding fell through: "this record does not re-fetch the URL itself as a command, so the citation's exact current text is not re-verified by anything in commands[] above; it is asserted from what was read earlier in this session." That disclosure is correct, and it is what let me find this quickly. It is also, now measured, not a theoretical caveat: re-fetching would have caught claim (b).

== NEAR-MISS I CAUGHT AND AM PRINTING RATHER THAN HIDING ==

CI on this head shows the `test` job failing on all six matrix legs, and its log carries "FAIL: proof/39.json: python3 scripts/lwb_handoff.py --check: digest mismatch". Commit 5fa8e75 regenerates HANDOFF.md, and proof/39.json's recorded tail is "OK: <repo>/HANDOFF.md passes all checks (2961 bytes)" -- so the obvious and wrong reading is that this PR's HANDOFF regeneration invalidated a recorded digest. I nearly wrote that up as a second blocking finding.

It is not this PR's. I ran scripts/lwb_check_proof.py --reexecute on an untouched origin/main worktree (0d1be714): it fails there too, identically, on the same proof/39.json command -- main's HANDOFF.md is 2960 bytes against a recorded 2961. The mismatch is PRE-EXISTING on main and this PR only changes which wrong byte count is reported. Separately, I misread the blast radius before checking: ci.yml's lwb-proof-reexecute step is `continue-on-error: true`, deliberately report-only, so the digest mismatch cannot fail the job at all. The `test` job's actual exit-1 is the LAST step, lwb-lanes: "5fa8e75100db: touches a shared path and has 0 independent review(s) in reviews/70/, needs 1" -- i.e. the missing record this file supplies. Two separate errors I would have shipped had I stopped at the log.

FORWARD-LOOKING, not this PR's to fix: PR #62 makes lwb-proof-reexecute blocking. If #62 lands while proof/39.json's digest is stale on main, main goes red. Recommend re-recording proof/39.json's handoff digest, or making that command non-verifiable, before #62 merges.

== TRIAGE NOTE: a false-accusation trap in my own dispatch instructions ==

My instructions say to skip a PR whose reviews/<pr>/ holds a record whose reviewed_commit equals the CURRENT HEAD SHA. Applied literally, all 14 open PRs look unreviewed, because committing a record advances the raw head past the sha the record names. The gate does not compare against the raw head: resolve_reviewable_head in scripts/lwb_lanes.py skips commits touching only reviews/ and proof/. Comparing against the REVIEWABLE head instead, 13 of 14 open PRs already carry a current AGREE, and only #70 genuinely lacked one. Had I followed the instruction as written I would have re-reviewed 13 PRs and filed 13 redundant records. Recording it so the next run does not have to rediscover it. (Reviewer A's PR #69 record reaches the same conclusion independently.)

Caveat on that triage: I replicated resolve_reviewable_head with `git log --format=%H <head>`, matching main's current all-parents walk. PR #63 changes that walk to --first-parent. My triage would differ from a post-#63 gate on any branch with a merge whose side history contains non-record commits. It does not affect #70, which has no merges and whose reviewable head equals its raw head.
